articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Sean Payton not a cure-all for Broncos fantasy woes
articles.description: Sean Payton will call the plays for the Broncos offense, but fantasy managers should temper their expectations.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 8: Sean Payton is not a cure-all for Broncos' fantasy woes

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

It'd be understandable if fantasy managers of Denver Broncos players are giddy with excitement following the news that head coach Sean Payton is taking back playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb.

These Broncos, who finished 10th in yardage and 14th in scoring last season, have seen those rankings dip to 27th in either category in 2026. Bo Nix is only the No. 20 quarterback in terms of fantasy scoring, and much ballyhooed offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle is 33th among wide receivers. And don't get any of us started on Courtland Sutton or the top two running backs, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

But here's the reality of the situation: Playcalling changes don't always lend immediate, dramatic results, and this year's returns thus far might be as much of an indication of Nix's raw talent than it is the playcalling.

Sure, under Webb's direction, the Broncos' offense has been more conservative, forcing Nix to rely much more on dump-offs and screens. And perhaps Payton, who coaxed decently productive seasons from the 26-year-old quarterback in 2024 and 2025, will open things up more, raising Nix's ceiling for softer matchups and getting the ball to Waddle with more space to make things happen after the catch.

To the latter point, Waddle's average depth of target is down more than two full yards this season, and he's on pace for 51 targets within five yards of, or behind, the line of scrimmage, which would be easily his most since his rookie 2021. I'd love to see him exploited more in the deep game, raising his ceiling into the mid-to-high range of fantasy WR2s, but it's hardly a guarantee that this coaching move will make it happen. Waddle is slightly more attractive a trade target -- and this speaks to those of you off to slow starts in need of shaking things up with higher-upside moves -- but I'm not making rash adjustments to my valuations.

As is, it hasn't been the easiest of schedules for Payton's Broncos (@KC, JAX, LAR, @SF), and things do ease up with Los Angeles Chargers (Week 5) and Arizona Cardinals (Week 7) matchups upcoming. Their second-half schedule is better than the first as well. That's as much of an actionable on the trade front for Broncos players, but it's also not something that should dramatically swing the arrow upward.

articles.headline: Tyreek Hill testifies in assault and battery civil trial in Miami
articles.description: Tyreek Hill took the stand in his assault and battery civil trial Thursday. He denied allegations that he ever physically abused his estranged wife.
articles.body:
MIAMI -- Tyreek Hill took the stand in his assault and battery civil trial Thursday, saying he was "deeply ashamed" for having threatened his wife's safety by saying he was "able to get people to hurt her." But the former NFL All-Pro wide receiver denied allegations that he ever physically abused his estranged wife.

The testimony came on the third day of the Miami civil case filed by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro.

"I wish I could have handled that situation a whole lot better," Hill said about one of several 2024 arguments the two had. "I wish I could have, you know, talked to my wife better. ... I just wish I could just take it all back."

The NFL says it is currently reviewing Hill's personal conduct, while his agent told ESPN that Hill could be close to negotiating a new NFL contract after recovering from knee surgery.

Hill, dressed in a light color knit sport shirt with an earring dangling from his right ear, told jurors he made the statement to his wife "in the heat of the moment" and that he had no intention of hurting her.

His attorney asked whether he ever hit, scratched or shoved Vaccaro, pulled out her hair, spit in her face or punched toward her stomach while she was pregnant, as Vaccaro alleged in sworn testimony. Hill denied each allegation.

Vaccaro previously testified that Hill left her on the side of the road after a May 2024 event, and she ordered a car service to get her home. Hill told jurors Vaccaro demanded to be let out of the car, and he complied but said he waited as her car service arrived and followed it back to the couple's home.

During the nearly two hours of direct testimony, Hill repeatedly denied abusive behavior and claimed that most of their disagreements surrounded financial concerns he had with respect to a post-nuptial agreement he claims she would not sign. He also accused Vaccaro of stealing money from a family bank account even though he had given her access to a "family card" for household purchases such as groceries.

"She was stealing money during the marriage," said Hill. "She was getting $15K [a month], but she was stealing around like $60K a month. And I would see that, and then I would say something."

Hill also testified about the final fight the couple had before Vaccaro filed for divorce in April 2025. The couple's nanny camera recorded audio and video of the encounter, which was played before the jury.

The nanny camera recorded expletives repeated between the couple and Vaccaro screaming at Hill to "stop." At one point in the video, Hill is heard saying "I'm going to get my daughter and get the f--- out." Hill is seen on the camera taking his daughter out of her crib as she wakes up from a nap.

Vaccaro's mother was in the condominium at the time and testified earlier Thursday to what she witnessed and heard. The mother said she never saw Hill physically abuse her daughter at any time.

articles.headline: NFL Week 5 uniforms: Packers debut Rivalries look, Patriots wearing throwbacks
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 5, led by the Green Bay Packers debuting their Rivalries look.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers have had their fair share of alternate uniforms throughout their distinguished history. There were the 1950s all-green look and the 1923 classic threads unveiled last year. However, no Packers combination has ever been like the ones they'll wear this week.

Green Bay will debut its "Rivalries" uniforms against the Chicago Bears on Sunday. It's a look that includes a desaturated vintage green jersey with alabaster pants and a matching matte helmet. The alabaster color is reminiscent of the aged paper of historic Packers stock certificates, according to the team. With the franchise being publicly owned, fans are able to become shareholders. More than 500,000 homes in Wisconsin include framed stock certificates, which inspired the uniform design. The alabaster jersey numbers feature an engraved treatment modeled after the lettering of paper currency -- a nod to financial support for the team. "Go Pack Go" runs on the back of the helmet, while "Making History Since 1919" is inside the collar. 

In throwback fashion, the New England Patriots are wearing their "Pat Patriot" look versus the Las Vegas Raiders. The red uniforms include tricolored shoulder stripes with white numbers. White pants and helmets complete the look with the star of the show being Pat Patriot on the lid.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Category league draft tiers
articles.description: Eric Moody groups players into tiers by each position for category-based leagues.
articles.body:
Category leagues require a different approach than points leagues. Volume still matters, but it isn't everything. Steals and blocks are harder to find, while 3-pointers can be concentrated among certain types of players. Field goal percentage, free throw percentage and turnovers can quietly swing a league over the course of a season.

That can change how players should be valued.

A guard who gives you steals, 3-pointers and strong percentages can be more valuable than a higher-scoring player who hurts you elsewhere. A center who blocks shots without wrecking your free throw percentage can give you a major advantage. A forward who provides assists can help solve a shortage in a category that is harder to address at that position.

Our recent 10-team roto mock showed how that can play out. Four point guards went in the first round, while no small forwards were selected. Then Cooper Flagg, Scottie Barnes and Amen Thompson went with three of the first four picks of Round 2. Point guard became a focus again in Round 3, when James Harden, Jalen Brunson, Josh Giddey, LaMelo Ball, Jamal Murray and Stephen Curry all came off the board in a seven-pick span.

Derrick White also went 17th overall, which makes sense given how difficult his combination of 3s, assists, steals and blocks is to replace at shooting guard. Power forward showed one of the clearest positional drop-offs, while center remained deep enough that useful rebounders and shot-blockers were still available well into the middle rounds.

That's where tiers become useful.

I've separated players by their default position, even if they qualify at multiple spots. The rankings show how I value the players in a neutral build. The tiers show where the player pool changes. Once the draft starts, what you already have should influence what comes next.

The goal isn't simply to draft the highest-ranked player every round. It's to know from round to round what your team does well, where it is vulnerable and when a category or position is about to become much harder to draft.

The rankings tell you who I like. The tiers tell you when you need to act. Your roster tells you who fits best.

To see points league draft tiers, click here.

See more:  Sign up | Rankings | Projections | Mock Draft Lobby

Gilgeous-Alexander and Doncic are the clear top two, but they give category managers very different foundations. Gilgeous-Alexander is projected for 31.3 PPG while shooting 53.6% from the field and 88.3% from the line, with 1.7 SPG and only 2.3 turnovers a game. You get elite scoring without taking a major hit elsewhere. Doncic gives you even more volume in points, 3s, rebounds and assists, but his projected 78.3% free throw shooting and 4.0 turnover average have to be managed.

articles.headline: Cards' Marvin Harrison Jr. paying 'no mind' to trade rumors
articles.description: Sources said the Cardinals are not shopping Marvin Harrison Jr. but other teams are still doing their due diligence on the receiver, including the Colts.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. said Thursday he isn't paying attention to the trade rumors swirling around him.

Speculation that the No. 4 pick in the 2024 NFL draft could be moved by the Nov. 10 trade deadline heated up in the past few weeks. Helping fuel that speculation is Harrison's decision to hire Todd France and Tory Dandy as his agents Sept. 23, according to the NFLPA online database. Harrison did not have an agent prior to then.

"Truthfully, I pay it no mind," Harrison said of the speculation. "I'm only focused on Detroit, helping the Cardinals win football games at the moment. So whatever rumors you're talking about, I don't pay it no mind."

Sources told ESPN that the Cardinals are not shopping Harrison but other teams are still doing their due diligence on the third-year receiver. Those include the Colts, with a source telling ESPN that they would entertain the idea of trading for Harrison, the son of Marvin Harrison Sr., the Hall of Famer who owns multiple Indianapolis receiving records.

The Colts placed No. 1 receiver Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve last month and are hopeful he can return later this season. Without him, Indianapolis has struggled to create explosive plays on offense. The team recently signed former New York Giants receiver Darius Slayton to help at the position.

Harrison has five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown through four games this season. His 12 targets are the fifth most on the Cardinals; tight end Trey McBride, wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne and running back Jeremiyah Love all have more.

Harrison's only touchdown of the season came in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants at MetLife Stadium. After he scored, while sitting on the turf, he raised his right index finger to the mouth area of his facemask to indicate a shush motion.

Asked Thursday about what message he wanted to get across with the celebration, Harrison said: "No message."

After Sunday's game, coach Mike LaFleur said he still has faith in Harrison.

"Yeah, my confidence is high in Marv," LaFleur said.

articles.headline: Bills' 'one-of-a-kind' Josh Allen offers challenge for Rams' defensive progress on Monday night
articles.description: — From his sideline, Matthew Stafford had a great vantage point on Josh Allen’s skills as the Los Angeles Rams held off the Buffalo Bills 44-42 on Dec. 8, 2024, when Allen became the
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — From his sideline, Matthew Stafford had a great vantage point on Josh Allen’s skills as the Los Angeles Rams held off the Buffalo Bills 44-42 on Dec. 8, 2024, when Allen became the first player in the Super Bowl era to run for three touchdowns and pass for three TDs in a game.


              “He’s a one-of-a-kind type player at the quarterback position,” Stafford said. “I think size, speed, ability to throw the ball, all the things you’d want. So he’s a big-time player. It’s fun to watch.”


              Allen is decidedly less enjoyable to try to defend, as the other side of the ball for the Rams (2-2) will have to do in their showdown with the Bills (3-1) on Monday night.


              “He’s probably a lot more fun when you don’t got to tackle him,” Rams defensive end Braden Fiske said. “But, hey, anytime you get to compete against the best, it is fun.”


              Allen accounted for 342 yards passing and 82 yards rushing without a turnover in his memorable last visit to SoFi Stadium, coming up short after trailing by 17 points twice in the third quarter. Those offensive fireworks happened in nine possessions while possessing the ball for just 21:30. 


              Buffalo coach Joe Brady, who was Allen’s offensive coordinator at the time, could only remember the things that went wrong.


              “We dug ourselves a hole in that game, and it allowed it to get to that point,” Brady said. “You guys know how I am. I have such a high standard, so I’m always gonna reflect on the bad. But it didn’t have to get to that point that it did.”


              The Rams’ defensive players are looking forward to the challenge as a chance to measure where they are at after an up-and-down first month of the season. Los Angeles ranks second in the NFL in total yards (247.5) and yards passing allowed (145.5), having smothered the New York Giants after starting quarterback Jaxson Dart was hurt and putting the clamps on the Philadelphia Eagles, while also struggling to contain the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos.


              “As a football fan, man, I respect his game a lot,” Rams cornerback Jaylen McCollough said of Allen. “You know, he’s a generational talent.”

articles.headline: Thunder's Gilegous-Alexander buys stake in Atlético Madrid
articles.description: Two-time NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has become a shareholder in Atlético Madrid, the Spanish club announced on Thursday.
articles.body:
Two-time NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has become a shareholder in Atlético Madrid, the Spanish club announced on Thursday.

In a statement, Atlético, who are currently second in LaLiga, said their partnership with the Oklahoma City Thunder guard, 28, was "grounded in shared values: ambition, excellence and the belief that every result must be earned."

Atlético have been majority owned by the US-based fund Apollo Global Management since last year.

"I'm excited to officially join Atlético Madrid's ownership group," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "This is a club with a long-standing presence at the top of European football, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

The club did not disclose the size of Gilgeous-Alexander's ownership stake.

The Canadian, who was pictured wearing an Atlético tracksuit earlier this year, was traded to the Thunder in 2019, after spending a season with the LA Clippers.

He won the 2025 NBA finals, being named MVP, and won his second MVP title a year later as the Thunder were eliminated in the Western Conference Finals.

Gilgeous-Alexander also played for Canada at the 2024 Olympics.

Atlético are one of Spain's most successful football clubs, most recently winning LaLiga in 2014 and 2021 under current coach Diego Simeone.

Gilgeous-Alexander joins a number of high-profile NBA players who have invested in football, including LeBron James and Kevin Durant.

articles.headline: Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe make 'Abbott Elementary' cameos
articles.description: "Abbott Elementary" continues to embrace Philadelphia sports culture with its latest instance starring the 76ers.
articles.body:
Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Jaylen Brown made a surprise appearance on the season premiere of "Abbott Elementary" on Wednesday night, but their visit to the fictional Philadelphia school didn't exactly go as planned.

The cameo occurred during a scene in which history teacher Jacob Hill (played by Chris Perfetti) made an Instagram post asking the Philadelphia 76ers to build a playground at Abbott Elementary. Hill had learned that the Philadelphia Eagles build a free playground for a local school each year, but the team had already selected another school.

After a group of impostors wearing Sixers jerseys convinced Hill they were bench players for the team, the real NBA stars arrived to answer his request. 

Maxey introduced himself, Edgecombe and the team's "new guy," Brown, telling Hill that he'd seen his Instagram post and found it "very effective."

There was just one problem: Hill, who isn't particularly familiar with men's sports, didn't recognize them.

"If you're the Sixers, then where's LeBron James?" Hill asked.

"This is going to sound like a lie, but he's actually running up the 'Rocky' steps right now," Maxey replied.

"He loves that movie," Brown added.

Unconvinced, Hill dismissed the trio.

"Yeah, right. Get the hell out of here, you tall jerks," he said.

As the players walked away, Hill made the admission:

"I really got to start watching men's sports."

Ahead of the Season 6 premiere, "Abbott Elementary" creator and star Quinta Brunson, a West Philadelphia native who plays second-grade teacher Janine Teagues, shared a photo with the three players on Instagram. Maxey responded in the comments with a goat emoji.

The NBA trio joins a growing list of Philadelphia sports figures who have appeared on the ABC comedy.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made a virtual appearance during the Season 3 premiere in February 2024, alongside former teammates Jason Kelce and Brandon Graham. Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith has also appeared on the show.

Philadelphia Phillies slugger Kyle Schwarber appeared in an episode filmed at Citizens Bank Park last season, while Philadelphia Flyers mascot Gritty was in the Season 2 premiere.

The Sixers have also been part of the show's storylines before. Brunson's character once dressed as former Philadelphia guard James Harden for Halloween, and the teachers competed for courtside Sixers tickets in a Season 2 episode. Former Sixers player Andre Iguodala also made an appearance as a fictional love interest of principal Ava Coleman (played by Janelle James).

articles.headline: Man City manager Enzo Maresca says he 'trusts the club completely'
articles.description: Enzo Maresca has said he "trusts the club completely" in his first interview since Manchester City were found guilty of breaking financial rules.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca has said he "trusts the club completely" in his first interview since Manchester City were found guilty of breaking financial rules.

Maresca is preparing his players for the trip to Liverpool on Sunday -- City's first game since the publication of the damning judgement in their case with the Premier League.

The Italian spoke to in-house media on Thursday. He's due to hold his first news conference with reporters since the verdict on Friday morning.

"Personally, I'm very calm to be honest," said Maresca.

"The club has been quite clear. We trust completely the club.

"We understand the noise, but the focus for us is just what we can control and we can control just the football side."

Despite the guilty verdict, both chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano have insisted the club are innocent. A formal appeal has been launched.

The bulk of City's players have been away on international duty during the break. Now back at the CFA, Maresca insists they are "focused" despite intense spotlight on the Etihad Stadium.

"The feeling is fantastic, to be honest," Maresca said.

"The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league.

"The players are just focused on that. They know what we can control is the football side -- they are not worried at all about different things.

"They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don't care too much about the noise. They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield."

articles.headline: Sources: 76ers plan to play starters in preseason game vs. Nets
articles.description: The 76ers plan to play their starters Thursday against the Nets, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Philadelphia 76ers plan to play their starters Thursday against the Brooklyn Nets, sources told ESPN, giving fans a first preseason glimpse of LeBron James in a Sixers uniform.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse told reporters that if all of his main players came through Wednesday's practice healthy, he hoped to play "the majority" of them -- namely James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe -- together in the first half against the Nets.

James, Embiid and Maxey were healthy scratches in Philadelphia's preseason-opening victory Monday against the New York Knicks.

Brown scored 22 points in 17 minutes Monday while Edgecombe had 12 points and seven assists in 20 minutes.

articles.headline: Mourinho jokes he'll be lucky to still be around when Man City case ends
articles.description: Real Madrid coach José Mourinho joked that he'll be lucky to still be around to see the final verdict in the Premier League's case against Manchester City.
articles.body:
Real Madrid coach José Mourinho joked that he'll be lucky to still be around to see the final verdict in the Premier League's case against Manchester City.

An independent commission's verdict published last week found City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. It detailed how City arranged "sham" commercial deals to inflate revenues and reduce costs by £900 million ($1.2b billion) during a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

- What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

- Haaland: City must 'stay positive' amid PL case

- Man City's Maresca 'trusts the club completely'

The verdict came 21 months after the culmination of a 12-week hearing, following an investigative process that dates back to 2019.

However, City have appealed the verdict and say they have "irrefutable evidence" of their innocence.

And Mourinho, who led Manchester United to second place in the Premier League behind City in 2017-18, said he is not holding his breath waiting for the case to come to its conclusion.

"I would rather laugh about ‌it," ⁠Mourinho said of the case during an interview with Italian publication Corriere dello Sport. "I think we will eventually get an ending, but we are both in our 60s and we'll need ​to be lucky ​enough to still ⁠be around when the final verdict arrives.

"There will be a verdict, then appeals, then more appeals."

Mourinho has previously said that he may still receive a winners' medal if City are stripped of the prize.

The Premier League said that City's appeal to an independent appeal board "will remain private and confidential until publication of the outcome is permitted."

Fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions are among "a broad discretion" of sanctions available to the commission, the Premier League also said.

ESPN has reported that a timeframe is in place for City's fate to be resolved by the end of this season.

But City could yet take the case beyond sporting regulatory bodies to the High Court in the United Kingdom if the appeal fails and City can prove serious irregularities in the Premier League's disciplinary process.

Information from ESPN's Mark Ogden was used in this report.

articles.headline: Tottenham's Xavi Simons enrolls at Harvard Business School
articles.description: Tottenham Hotspur's Xavi Simons has revealed he has enrolled for an online course at Harvard Business School.
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur's Xavi Simons has revealed he has enrolled for an online course at Harvard Business School. 

Simons, 23, said in a post on LinkedIn that he had been accepted onto the Crossover Into Business Program at the graduate business school of the Ivy League university in the United States.

The Netherlands international is currently recovering from an ACL tear suffered during the run-in at the end of last season when Spurs narrowly avoided being relegated from the Premier League. 

A timeline for Simons' return to action is unclear, but he is not expected to be match fit until at least the beginning of 2027.

He has been spending time in the U.S. while rehabilitating, posting photos on Instagram of him with basketball star Jay Tatum and watching a USC vs. Oregon college football game. 

The Harvard Business School website says it has delivered the Crossover Into Business course to at least 20 athletes from the NBA, WNBA, NFL, MLS, NWSL and the UFC.

"I'm going back to school," Simons wrote in the post. 

"During my recovery, I've been trying to use my time in the best way possible. Football is still my main focus, but I also want to keep learning and improving away from the pitch.

"I'm happy to share that I've been accepted onto the Crossover Into Business Program at Harvard Business School. It's an online program where professional athletes learn more about business alongside HBS MBA students.

"I've always been interested in more than just football. I want to understand the business side of the game better, learn from people in different industries and keep developing as a person.

"Over the last few weeks, I've spent time on both the East Coast and West Coast in the U.S., meeting new people and seeing different ways of working. It's given me a lot of new ideas. It also makes this experience extra special because of Professor Anita Elberse. We first met during my time at FC Barcelona, and later again at Paris Saint-Germain. We've stayed in touch over the years, so it was great to see her again and visit Harvard while I was in Boston.

"Getting back on the pitch is still my number one priority. At the same time, I want to use this period to keep learning and invest in myself beyond football."

Tottenham face Manchester United in their next Premier League fixture on Saturday.

articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタは、5月に行われたパリ・サンジェルマンとのチャンピオンズリーグ決勝での敗戦による「傷跡」がいまだに残っていると語った。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.
